### Summary

Toon's solver replaces the angular field by two hemispheric fluxes and solves the resulting pair of linear
differential equations exactly in every homogeneous layer. Its fluxes therefore differ from the true ones for two
separate reasons: the round-off of solving those equations, and the approximation of replacing many directions by
two. This section measures both on the chapter's grid. The first is at round-off; the second is up to
$8.7\times10^{-2}$ of the incident flux, with a median of $1.1\times10^{-3}$. The section closes with tolerances for
pyharp's tests that follow from these numbers, and with one input on which the solver fails: a single-scattering
albedo of exactly one.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Split Toon's flux error into numerical and approximation parts, @eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-split.

**Data.** Toon and DISORT fluxes on the grid of @sec-ch05-reference.

**Placement.** A measurement on the solver; nothing in pyharp runs it.

**Activation.** `solver: toon` in the band YAML; `flags` for thermal options.

**Guarantee / limits.** Round-off for $\omega < 1$; wrong at $\omega = 1$ exactly.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

Local symbols: $e^{\mathrm{num}}$, $e^{\mathrm{app}}$, $e^{\mathrm{tot}}$ the numerical, approximation and total
flux errors [-]; $r$ the fractional error [-]; $\mathsf M$ the $3\times3$ matrix of the shortwave system [-];
$\mathbf v$ its state vector; $x$ the unknown upward flux at the top. The two-stream symbols $\gamma_1$ to
$\gamma_4$, $\lambda$ and $\Gamma$, the scaled variables $\omega'$, $\tau'$, $g'$, and the margin $\delta\omega$ are
those of the ch2 notation.

These tolerances are proposed for `tests/test_toon.py` in place of the 20 % gate against 4-stream DISORT: 10 % on
shortwave fluxes against DISORT at 64 streams, $10^{-5}$ on non-scattering thermal fluxes, 5 % on scattering thermal
fluxes, and a new numerical gate of $10^{-12}$ against the exact two-stream solution. The Tests layer gives the
measurement behind each.

### Derivation

**The equations Toon solves.** In each layer pyharp first applies the $\delta$-Eddington scaling, which moves the
forward peak of the phase function into the direct beam [@reading06]:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\omega' &= \frac{(1-g^2)\,\omega}{1-\omega g^2} \\
\Delta\tau' &= (1-\omega g^2)\,\Delta\tau \\
g' &= \frac{g}{1+g} ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-scaling}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-scaling check_ch05_toon_vs_disort.py [C1] -->
<!-- equation-source: eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-scaling delta-Eddington scaling of Joseph et al. 1976 -->

with $\Delta\tau$ [-] the layer optical thickness. It then uses the quadrature closure of Toon et al.
[@reading02, Table 1, p. 16,289], with $\mu_0$ the cosine of the solar zenith angle:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\gamma_1 &= \tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\,\bigl(2 - \omega'(1+g')\bigr) \\
\gamma_2 &= \tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\,\omega'(1-g') \\
\gamma_3 &= \tfrac12\,\bigl(1 - \sqrt3\, g'\mu_0\bigr) \\
\gamma_4 &= 1 - \gamma_3 .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-gamma}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-gamma check_ch05_toon_vs_disort.py [C1] -->
<!-- equation-source: eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-gamma Toon et al. 1989, Table 1 -->

@eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-scaling and @eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-gamma are computed in `toon_mckay89_shortwave`
({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_shortwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_shortwave repo=pyharp >}}). With $\tau'$ the scaled optical
depth from the top, the diffuse fluxes then obey [@reading02, eqs. 11-14, p. 16,289]

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathrm{d}F^{+}}{\mathrm{d}\tau'} &= \gamma_1 F^{+} - \gamma_2 F^{-} - \gamma_3\,\omega' F_0\, e^{-\tau'/\mu_0} \\
\frac{\mathrm{d}F^{-}}{\mathrm{d}\tau'} &= \gamma_2 F^{+} - \gamma_1 F^{-} + \gamma_4\,\omega' F_0\, e^{-\tau'/\mu_0} ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-ode}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-ode check_ch05_toon_vs_disort.py [C1] -->
<!-- equation-source: eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-ode Toon et al. 1989, eqs. 11-14 -->

with no diffuse radiation entering at the top, $F^{-}(0) = 0$, and a Lambertian surface at $\tau_0'$,
$F^{+}(\tau_0') = A_s\bigl(F^{-}(\tau_0') + \mu_0 F_0\, e^{-\tau_0'/\mu_0}\bigr)$. pyharp solves
@eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-ode layer by layer with exponentials $e^{\pm\lambda\tau'}$, $\lambda^2 = \gamma_1^2 - \gamma_2^2$,
joined by a tridiagonal system (`toon_mckay89_shortwave`,
{{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_shortwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_shortwave repo=pyharp >}}); the solution method itself is the
subject of the Toon chapter.

**An independent exact solution.** For a homogeneous slab, collect $\mathbf v = (F^{+}, F^{-}, e^{-\tau'/\mu_0})$
with $F_0 = 1$. @eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-ode becomes the linear system $\mathrm{d}\mathbf v/\mathrm{d}\tau' =
\mathsf M\,\mathbf v$, with

$$
\mathsf M = \begin{pmatrix} \gamma_1 & -\gamma_2 & -\gamma_3\,\omega' \\ \gamma_2 & -\gamma_1 & \gamma_4\,\omega' \\ 0 & 0 & -1/\mu_0 \end{pmatrix} .
$$

Its solution from the top is $\mathbf v(\tau') = \exp(\mathsf M\tau')\,\mathbf v(0)$ with $\mathbf v(0) = (x, 0, 1)$,
where $x$ is the unknown upward flux at the top. Write $\mathsf P = \exp(\mathsf M\tau_0')$. The surface condition
is linear in $x$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_{11}x + P_{13} &= A_s\,\bigl(P_{21}x + P_{23} + \mu_0 P_{33}\bigr) \\
x &= -\frac{P_{13} - A_s P_{23} - A_s \mu_0 P_{33}}{P_{11} - A_s P_{21}} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-shoot}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-shoot check_ch05_toon_vs_disort.py [C1] -->

Shooting from the top amplifies round-off by $e^{\lambda\tau_0'}$, which reaches $e^{35}$ on the grid, so the check
evaluates @eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-shoot in 50-digit arithmetic (`exact_sw` in
`derivation-checks/check_ch05_toon_vs_disort.py`); the result is exact to double precision.

**The error split.** With $\hat F$ fluxes normalised by $F_{\mathrm{inc}}$ (@eq-ch05-reference-finc),

$$
\begin{aligned}
e^{\mathrm{tot}} &= \hat F_{\mathrm{Toon}} - \hat F_{\mathrm{DISORT}} \\
                 &= \bigl(\hat F_{\mathrm{Toon}} - \hat F_{\mathrm{exact}}\bigr) + \bigl(\hat F_{\mathrm{exact}} - \hat F_{\mathrm{DISORT}}\bigr) \\
                 &= e^{\mathrm{num}} + e^{\mathrm{app}} ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-split}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-split check_ch05_toon_vs_disort.py [C3] -->

where $\hat F_{\mathrm{exact}}$ solves @eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-ode exactly and $\hat F_{\mathrm{DISORT}}$ is the
reference of @sec-ch05-reference. The reference's own error, below $1.05\times10^{-5}$ by @eq-ch05-reference-bound,
is part of $e^{\mathrm{app}}$. Toon et al. judge accuracy by the fractional error relative to the exact value
[@reading02, p. 16,294]; on fluxes of at least 1 % of the incident flux it is

$$
r = \frac{|e^{\mathrm{tot}}|}{|\hat F_{\mathrm{DISORT}}|} .
$$ {#eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-frac}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-frac check_ch05_toon_vs_disort.py [C35] -->
<!-- equation-source: eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-frac fractional error of Toon et al. 1989, p. 16,294 -->

**Why $\omega = 1$ breaks the kernel.** At $\omega = 1$, @eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-scaling gives $\omega' = 1$ for any
$g$, and @eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-gamma gives $\gamma_1 = \gamma_2 = \tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}(1-g') \equiv \gamma$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lambda^2 &= \gamma_1^2 - \gamma_2^2 = 0 \\
\Gamma &= \frac{\gamma_1 - \lambda}{\gamma_2} = 1 .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-degenerate}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-degenerate check_ch05_toon_vs_disort.py [C2] -->

The homogeneous part of @eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-ode becomes $\mathrm{d}F^{\pm}/\mathrm{d}\tau' = \gamma\,(F^{+} -
F^{-})$. Subtracting the two lines gives $\mathrm{d}(F^{+} - F^{-})/\mathrm{d}\tau' = 0$, so its general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}
F^{+} - F^{-} &= c \\
F^{-} &= b + \gamma c\,\tau' ,
\end{aligned}
$$

with two constants $b$ and $c$. The kernel's basis is $F^{+} = k_1 e^{\lambda\tau'} + \Gamma k_2 e^{-\lambda\tau'}$,
$F^{-} = \Gamma k_1 e^{\lambda\tau'} + k_2 e^{-\lambda\tau'}$ [@reading02, eqs. 19-20, p. 16,290]. At
$\lambda = 0$ and $\Gamma = 1$ both terms are the constant $k_1 + k_2$, so the basis spans only $c = 0$: it has lost
the mode that carries a net diffuse flux. The two boundary conditions can then not both be met. Toon et al. avoid
the limit by taking $1 - \omega_0$ equal to ten times the machine precision [@reading02, p. 16,291];
`RadiationBandImpl::forward` clamps $\omega \le 1 - \delta\omega$ with $\delta\omega = 10^{-12}$ in double and
$10^{-6}$ in single precision ({{< code src/radiation/radiation_band.cpp RadiationBandImpl::forward repo=pyharp >}}), but the
kernel itself applies no margin. That the lost mode is the cause is read from the code; the measured symptom in the
Tests layer, equal upward and downward fluxes at every level, is what it predicts.

What is exact and what is truncated: @eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-shoot is exact; Toon's kernel is exact for
@eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-ode up to round-off for $\omega < 1$; the truncation is the two-stream closure, which
$e^{\mathrm{app}}$ measures. The check is `check_ch05_toon_vs_disort.py` (Tests layer).

**Thermal emission.** Toon's thermal kernel does not solve a two-stream equation for the fluxes it returns: it
uses the hemispheric-mean two-stream solution only for the scattering source and integrates the emergent radiance
over five Gauss directions [@reading02, eqs. 52-56, p. 16,293]. Its numerical part is therefore bounded in two
ways that need no exact solution: a homogeneous isothermal slab gives the same fluxes as one layer or as sixteen,
and its band Planck integral agrees with DISORT's on an opaque slab. Everything else in its error is approximation.

### Numerical method

Each column of the grid of @sec-ch05-reference is solved four ways: Toon's shortwave kernel; the exact solution
@eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-shoot at the levels $\tau' = 0$, $\tau_0'/2$, $\tau_0'$; DISORT at 64 streams (beam); and,
for thermal emission, Toon with `hard_surface` and with `hard_surface,delta_eddington_lw` against DISORT at
32 streams. Statistics are taken over all levels and both channels, per regime of optical depth and single-scattering
albedo.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch05-toon-accuracy-split
#| fig-cap: "Toon's shortwave flux error on the chapter grid, by regime of optical depth (thin: tau0 up to 0.1, mid: 0.3 to 1, thick: 3 and 10) and single-scattering albedo (low: up to 0.6; 0.9; high: 0.99 and 0.999). Vermillion bars: largest approximation error; hatched green bars: largest numerical error; open circles: median total error; all divided by the incident flux. The numerical part sits at 1e-15 in every regime, so the whole error is the two-stream approximation."
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart on a log axis from 1e-17 to 1. In each of nine regimes a tall bar near 3e-2 to 9e-2 for the approximation error, a short hatched bar near 1e-15 for the numerical error, and a circle between 1e-4 and 1e-2 for the median total error."
#| echo: false
from pyharp_report.ch05.figures.fig_toon_error_split import make_fig
make_fig()
```

@fig-ch05-toon-accuracy-split shows the split for the shortwave.

| regime | $\omega \le 0.6$ | $\omega = 0.9$ | $\omega = 0.99$ to $0.999$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $\tau_0 \le 0.1$ | $2.7\times10^{-2}$ / $1.5\times10^{-4}$ | $3.8\times10^{-2}$ / $2.6\times10^{-4}$ | $4.1\times10^{-2}$ / $2.6\times10^{-4}$ |
| $0.3 \le \tau_0 \le 1$ | $4.4\times10^{-2}$ / $3.6\times10^{-3}$ | $7.4\times10^{-2}$ / $3.7\times10^{-3}$ | $8.7\times10^{-2}$ / $3.4\times10^{-3}$ |
| $\tau_0 \ge 3$ | $2.6\times10^{-2}$ / $2.7\times10^{-4}$ | $5.2\times10^{-2}$ / $9.6\times10^{-3}$ | $6.4\times10^{-2}$ / $7.6\times10^{-3}$ |

: Toon's shortwave error by regime, as a fraction of the incident flux (largest / median over all levels and both channels). {#tbl-ch05-toon-accuracy-regimes}

### Code

@tbl-ch05-toon-accuracy-code lists the code the measurement runs through.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| shortwave kernel | {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_shortwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_shortwave repo=pyharp >}} | `toon_mckay89_shortwave` | `solver: toon` |
| thermal kernel | {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_longwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_longwave repo=pyharp >}} | `toon_mckay89_longwave` | `flags: planck` |
| boundary conditions, channels | {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89.cpp ToonMcKay89Impl::forward repo=pyharp >}} | `ToonMcKay89Impl::forward` | always |
| flag parsing | {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89.hpp ToonMcKay89OptionsImpl::has_flag repo=pyharp >}} | `has_flag` | `flags` |
| $\omega$ margin $\delta\omega$ | {{< code src/radiation/radiation_band.cpp RadiationBandImpl::forward repo=pyharp >}} | `RadiationBandImpl::forward` | always in a band |

: Code map of the Toon accuracy measurement. {#tbl-ch05-toon-accuracy-code}

1. `ToonMcKay89Impl::forward` checks the shapes of the properties and of `umu0`, `fbeam` and `albedo`, pads the
   properties to three channels, and calls the shortwave kernel, or the thermal kernel when the `planck` flag is set
   ({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89.cpp ToonMcKay89Impl::forward repo=pyharp >}}). The thermal path refuses a call without
   `temf`.
2. `toon_mckay89_shortwave` applies @eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-scaling and @eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-gamma, moves $\mu_0$
   off the resonance $\lambda\mu_0 = 1$ by $\sqrt{\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}}$ where needed, and solves the tridiagonal
   system ({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_shortwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_shortwave repo=pyharp >}}).
3. `has_flag` reads the comma-separated `flags` without regard to case or spaces
   ({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89.hpp ToonMcKay89OptionsImpl::has_flag repo=pyharp >}}); an unknown flag is ignored, not
   refused.

### Tests

@tbl-ch05-toon-accuracy-tests lists the checks and the pyharp tests.

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `check_ch05_toon_vs_disort.py` [C1] | $\max|e^{\mathrm{num}}|$, shortwave, $\omega < 1$ | $10^{-12}$ | 100 times the measured round-off, $2.7\times10^{-15}$ |
| `check_ch05_toon_vs_disort.py` [C61]-[C63] | thermal multi-layer invariance | $10^{-10}$ | round-off of the tridiagonal solve; measured $2.9\times10^{-13}$ |
| `check_ch05_toon_vs_disort.py` [C64]-[C65] | thermal Planck integrals, Toon against DISORT | $10^{-5}$ | measured $4.8\times10^{-7}$ |
| `check_ch05_gs85.py` [C14] | Toon against Toon et al. Table 4 | $6\times10^{-4}$ | half-unit of their third decimal |
| `tests/test_toon.py` (pytest) | `test_toon_sw_vs_disort`: surface flux ratio to 4-stream DISORT | 0.8 to 1.2 | not stated; proposal below |
| `tests/test_toon.py` (pytest) | `test_toon_lw_isothermal`, `test_toon_lw_isothermal_scattering` | 20 % | not stated; proposal below |

: Tests of Toon's accuracy. {#tbl-ch05-toon-accuracy-tests}

**Numerical part.** Over the 720 shortwave columns with $\omega < 1$, $\max|e^{\mathrm{num}}| = 2.7\times10^{-15}$
of the incident flux, and the largest fractional numerical error is $1.0\times10^{-13}$. Toon's kernel solves
@eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-ode to round-off, so $e^{\mathrm{tot}} = e^{\mathrm{app}}$ to every digit shown below. The
thermal kernel's multi-layer invariance holds to $2.9\times10^{-13}$ of $\pi B$, and its Planck integrals agree with
DISORT's to $4.8\times10^{-7}$ (300 K) and $4.2\times10^{-8}$ (200 K).[^ch05-toon-run]

**Approximation part, shortwave.** Over all fluxes with $\omega < 1$ the largest error is $8.65\times10^{-2}$ of
the incident flux and the median $1.06\times10^{-3}$; the fractional error of @eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-frac has median
$6.6\times10^{-3}$ and maximum 0.49. By regime the errors are those of @tbl-ch05-toon-accuracy-regimes.

At $\mu_0 = 0.2$ the median is $2.9\times10^{-3}$, at
$\mu_0 \ge 0.5$ it is $6.8\times10^{-4}$. For the boundary quantities the largest errors are $8.6\times10^{-2}$ in
reflectance, $8.7\times10^{-2}$ in transmitted flux and $5.5\times10^{-2}$ in column absorption. Of the 3569 fluxes
of at least 1 % of the incident flux, 461 have $r > 10\,\%$: 344 of them are upward fluxes and 243 are at
$\mu_0 = 0.2$. The largest, $r = 0.49$, is the mid-level upward flux of $0.018$ of the incident flux at
$\tau_0 = 10$, $\omega = 0.9$, $g = 0.85$, $\mu_0 = 0.2$.[^ch05-toon-run]

**Approximation part, thermal.** With `hard_surface`, the largest error is $4.8\times10^{-2}$ of $\pi B(300\,K)$ and
the median $6.5\times10^{-4}$; adding `delta_eddington_lw` lowers them to $3.5\times10^{-2}$ and $5.6\times10^{-4}$.
Without scattering the error is below $2\times10^{-4}$ for all optical depths. The largest error is in thick slabs
with $\omega = 0.9$ to $0.99$, where the fractional error reaches 0.12 (0.10 with `delta_eddington_lw`).[^ch05-toon-run]

**Against Toon et al.** On the five Garcia-Siewert problems, with the asymmetry parameters Toon et al. used (0.794
and 0.848) and $\omega = 1$ run at $1 - 10^{-12}$, pyharp reproduces the approximate reflected and diffusely
transmitted fluxes of their Table 4 [@reading02, p. 16,295] to every printed digit: the largest difference is
$3.5\times10^{-4}$. With $g = \chi_1$ of the benchmark moment table, Toon's errors against the exact Table 22 values
are 0.1 % to 8.6 %, except the diffuse transmission of the thick absorbing cloud (problem 5, $4.7\times10^{-7}$ of
the incident flux), which is off by 78 %.[^ch05-toon-gs] Toon et al. state that the errors "are typically less than
10 % unless the flux or heating rate is 1 % or less" of the incident flux [@reading02, p. 16,296]. On this grid
that holds for the median, not for every flux: 13 % of the fluxes above 1 % of the incident flux have errors above
10 %, almost all small upward fluxes at low sun and strong forward scattering.

**Tolerances for `tests/test_toon.py`.** Measured on the cases those tests run:[^ch05-toon-run]

- `test_toon_sw_vs_disort`: measured 9.2 % against 4 streams and 8.4 % against the reference; proposed 10 %,
  against DISORT at 64 streams, which covers 8.4 % while 4 streams is not converged.
- `test_toon_lw_isothermal`: measured $4.8\times10^{-7}$ against both; proposed $10^{-5}$, since only the Planck
  integrals differ.
- `test_toon_lw_isothermal_scattering`: measured 3.4 % against 4 streams and 3.5 % against the reference; proposed
  5 %.
- New, a numerical gate: measured $2.7\times10^{-15}$; proposed $10^{-12}$, 100 times round-off.

The thermal tolerance of 20 % hides any regression five orders of
magnitude below it. Only the numerical gate can see an implementation error smaller than the two-stream error.

All Toon measurements run on the CPU in double precision; CUDA is the subject of the GPU chapter.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- **Candidate defect: $\omega = 1$ exactly in a direct call.** `ToonMcKay89` called directly with $\omega = 1$
  returns equal upward and downward fluxes at every level. On the grid the error reaches 1.37 of the incident
  flux, and on the thick conservative cloud (problem 4) the diffuse transmission is 100 % off. A band run through
  `RadiationBandImpl::forward` is not affected, because it clamps $\omega$ first
  ({{< code src/radiation/radiation_band.cpp RadiationBandImpl::forward repo=pyharp >}}). The cause, the lost mode of
  @eq-ch05-toon-accuracy-degenerate, is read from the code. This is one run; it stays a candidate until a second, independent run agrees.[^ch05-toon-run]
- **Small upward fluxes at low sun.** Fractional errors reach 49 % on upward fluxes of 1 % to 5 % of the incident
  flux at $\mu_0 = 0.2$ and $g = 0.85$; tolerances on such fluxes must be absolute, not relative.
- **Reflecting surfaces.** Over a Lambertian surface Toon carries the reflected field with two streams and misses
  the exact upward flux by $6.2\times10^{-3}$ of the incident flux even without scattering (@sec-ch05-analytic), as
  Toon et al. note [@reading02, p. 16,291].
- **Not measured.** Inhomogeneous columns, the `zenith_correction` flag, `top_emission_flag` other than 0, thermal
  runs without `hard_surface` against DISORT, and single precision.
:::
